newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks slightly lower in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks slightly lower in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks trended weaker on moderate volume in early Tuesday morning trading, as investors took to the sidelines to reassess the Hang Seng Index's 266-point advance over the past two trading days, brokers said.

"Funds have already put new money into the market following the Fed's last FOMC meeting and blue chips are now looking slightly overbought," said Conal Sanjana, institutional sales director at Kerry Securities.
The Hang Seng Index eased 36.86 points to 11,865.57 in early trade on moderate volume of nearly HK$1 billion.
Index futures had also closed at a sizeable discount to the cash market on Monday and now the cash market is coming down to meet the futures, Sanjana said.
October futures were up 12 points at 11.852 in early trade.
But brokers were not fazed by the market's opening weakness and expected the index to trend sideways following the recent strong gains.
"Our clients are happy to hold at this level, but we are not recommending an increased weighting at this time," said Anthony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.

Brokers said they found confusing Morgan Stanley's decision on Monday to increase the Hong Kong weighting in its Asia Pacific (non-Japan) model portfolio to 35 percent from 20 percent, an three-quarters increase.

Most institutional investors have probably already made slight upward adjustments in their funds' Hong Kong weightings, but brokers said such a large increase as suggested by Morgan Stanley's move seemed impracticable, given the market's size and how much money would have to flow in.
Property stocks were leading the market down at the opening, and the commercial and industrial sector was also weak.
The finance sector bucked the trend, rising slightly on the back of a gain in Hang Seng Bank. The share made a new high of of HK$82.50 before easing to trade up HK$0.25 at HK$82.25.
HSBC Holdings was unchanged at HK$143.50.
In the property sector, Henderson Land and Sun Hung Kai Properties both eased HK$0.50 to HK$65.75 and HK$81.75. New World Development shed HK$0.35 to HK$40.30.
Swire Pacific came in for profit-taking after the share's recent strong run. The stock eased HK$0.50 to HK$68.75.
